units.translation: Hesychius omits the name of Aeschylus. The faulty accent λαμπουρίς [fox] in both grammarians was corrected by L. Dindorf in the Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 84 from Etym. M. p. 474, 2 σεσημείωται τρία [three are noted] (not oxytone like other words in ουρις [ouria]) λάμπουρις, ἡ ἀλώπηξ [lampouris, the fox], Τόμουρις ὄνομα πόλεως [Tomuris, name of a city], καὶ ἵππουρις [and hippouris]. After Aeschylus this word was used by Lycophron 344 1393.
ouria) lampouris, the fox, Tomuris, name of a city, and hippouris
where M has ἐλευθερίως λαμπρῶς ἰδεῖν [to see the light of freedom brightly]. Weilius corrected it.
The bright full moon shines in the middle of the shield
the bright circle of the sun
the bright rulers who bring winter and summer to mortals, conspicuous in the sky
the bright light of the sun
he seems to be blowing brightly toward the sunrise
and to see the bright light of freedom with friendly eyes from the dark veil
seeing a bright brow moving in the darkness
and by polluting bright water with mud you will never find a drink
M: to see the light of freedom brightly
for the sleeping mind is brightened by the eyes
brightly and not at all in riddles
and many torches were lit in the house
weeping for the torch-carrying rites around you, always neglected
not to shine a light for the poor
to escape notice, to be hidden
to escape notice, to be hidden
λάθοιεν [they might escape notice] is corrupt for λάχοιεν [they might obtain]. See λαγχάνω [to obtain by lot].
The same is λήθομαι [I forget], which see.
it is not possible to escape the eyes of light
for it does not escape my notice, being clear
the eye of a young woman, blazing, will not escape my notice
lest he escape notice, having gone in flight
lest I escape notice, having died unexpectedly by a spear-wrought fate
let it not escape notice in any way
what is not lawful, trampled with the foot on the ground (Hermann: on the ground)
I see all these things trampled underfoot
revere the altar of Justice, and do not, seeing gain, dishonor it with godless foot by trampling
The word is corrupt. The meter requires νεοπαθέα [newly suffering], which Paleius conjectured, or another word of this measure.
revering the people-suffering and sea-beaten burdens
in the plural λαοί [peoples] assembled men
for the army of the Persians is unapproachable and the people valiant
for the people are freed to speak freely
the whole people has been destroyed by the spear
he acquired the people of the Lydians and Phrygians
the people of the Ionians, not fleeing from the spear
let the people be concerned to work out remedies in common
